main.title: Make Matter Matter.

1.title: It started with one act of fury.
1.copy: In 2021, watching Japanese entrepreneurs, we wrote something down. There are people who can compete globally. There is excellent technology. And still, that value never reaches the world.
1.quoteBefore: ...this club's stance of make themselves notable around the globe is astonishingly weak.
1.quoteAfter: Why the most of Japanese elites doesn't have the ambition to rule the world?

2.title: We went out into the world and learned what stood in the way.
2.copy: San Francisco, Denver, Bangkok. Not as attendees, but as builders. We learned firsthand what the walls were made of: language, borders, information, networks.
2.imgLgAlt: A view over the ETH San Francisco venue
2.imgSm1Alt: The entrance to the ETH Denver venue
2.imgSm2Alt: Group photo in front of the I DEMOED wall at ETHGlobal Bangkok

3.title: We built spaces and walked across Japan.
3.copy: A symposium in Ishigaki made the local paper; a sake brewery in Kagawa let us touch the memory held in the land. Value isn't scarce -- it just isn't found, told, or met.
3.imgLgAlt: Kazuma Tamura speaking on a DAO panel at ETHTokyo
3.imgSm1Alt: Speaking surrounded by tanks at a sake brewery in Kagawa
3.imgSm2Alt: Newspaper coverage of a web3.0 symposium in the Yaeyama Nippo

4.title: We built the place to meet.
4.copy: Our own international conference. At Google for Startups Campus Tokyo, we put builders from abroad and Japanese companies in the same room.
4.imgLgAlt: The full venue and group photo of speakers and attendees at FA1RNESS 2024

5.title: What we'd been searching for in the digital world, we found in a small factory.
5.copy: Ota Ward's small factories had "nakama-mawashi" -- the distributed collaboration we'd chased across the DAO world had been running as a real industry in Japanese manufacturing for decades. That's where A-one road's path came together into one line.
5.imgLgAlt: Visiting a craftsman at work in a small factory in Ota Ward
5.imgSmAlt: A workshop covered in whiteboard notes

main.title: Before we work together.

1.question: Is exclusivity required?
1.answer: The standard cooperation model is designed around non-exclusive distribution. Territory, rights and coordination with existing channels are defined in the MSA and SOW.

2.question: Which products can participate?
2.answer: Equipment, materials and technologies supporting manufacturing are considered. We review applications, supply capability and Japan-market fit across strategic and complementary areas.

3.question: What are the fees and timeline?
3.answer: A proposal is based on products, source materials, listing channels and scope. Launch follows contract execution, initial payment, material delivery and OEM approval.

4.question: Who handles installation, warranty and technical support?
4.answer: The OEM, A-one road and any logistics or technical providers have responsibilities defined per transaction. Additional technical work is quoted and agreed through a project SOW.

5.question: What materials should we prepare?
5.answer: Prepare specifications, applications, product images or catalogs, certification information, supply terms and a technical contact. Public-facing content is reviewed by the OEM.

main.title: Planning your procurement.

1.question: Can we inquire before selecting a machine?
1.answer: Yes. Share the part, material, current process and quality goals. We can discuss candidate technologies and confirm availability and suitability.

2.question: Can we ask about products outside the listed technology examples?
2.answer: The technology areas are selection guidelines. Distribution rights, supply terms and local support for a specific product are confirmed individually.

3.question: Are installation and maintenance included?
3.answer: Required work and responsible parties are stated in the quotation and contract. Evaluation, installation, process integration and maintenance are scoped as needed.

main.title:
A VAD foundation.
Three strategic technology areas.
main.copy: We focus our learning on versatile production equipment, scarce advanced processes and recurring materials used in manufacturing.

1.title: General Purpose
1.subtitle: Versatile production capability
1.copy: NC lathes and CNC machining centers: a foundation for diverse parts and materials, including aluminum, magnesium and copper.

2.title: Scarce Advanced
2.subtitle: Advanced and scarce capability
2.copy: LFAM, WAAM, CFRP, CNT and specialty alloys: options for large parts, complex geometries, new materials and advanced processes.

3.title: Feedstock & Materials
3.subtitle: Recurring manufacturing inputs
3.copy: Metal powders, wire, polymers and composite feedstocks: materials and application knowledge that support equipment operation and quality.

main.title: An entry point for complementary technologies.
main.copy: Machine vision, welding automation and industrial software can also enter through our VAD model. We review product fit, customers and service scope in an initial discussion.
